q: 1. In a precision traverse, included angles are measured by setting the vernier ...............
options: to read zero exactly on back station
to read 5° exactly on back station
somewhere near zero and reading both verniers on back station
explain: In high-precision work, instead of setting to exactly zero, it's better to read the actual initial readings on both verniers to eliminate setting errors.

q: 2. Closed traverse is suitable in the survey of
explain: A closed traverse, which returns to its starting point, is suitable for surveying areas that form a closed loop, like the boundary of a pond/lake; rivers, roads and coastlines are elongated features better surveyed by open traverses.

q: 3. If the angular measurements of a traverse are more precise than its linear measurements, balancing of the traverse, is done by
explain: The Transit rule is used to balance a traverse when angular measurements are considered more precise/reliable than the linear measurements, since it corrects latitudes and departures independently in proportion to their own magnitudes rather than the total leg length.

q: 4. The projection of a traverse line on a line perpendicular to the meridian is known as
explain: Departure is the projection of a line on the East-West axis (perpendicular to the North-South meridian).

q: 5. The process of turning the telescope about the vertical axis in horizontal plane is known as
explain: Swinging is the rotation of the theodolite telescope in a horizontal plane. Turning it in a vertical plane is called transiting or plunging.

q: 6. A traverse survey can be plotted
options: by rectangular coordinates or plotting by tangents
by paper protractor or by included angles
by parallel meridian method or plotting by chords
explain: All the mentioned methods are valid ways to transfer field traverse data onto paper.

q: 7. In measuring horizontal angles, the theodolite should be turned
options: clockwise from the forward station to the back station
clockwise from the back station to the forward station
anticlockwise from the back station to the forward station
anticlockwise from the forward station to the back station
explain: Standard practice for measuring horizontal angles with a theodolite is to sight the back station, set the scale, and then turn the instrument clockwise to the forward station.

q: 8. Which of the following methods of theodolite traversing is suitable for locating the details which are far away from transit stations?
options: by measuring angle to the point from at least three stations
by measuring angles to the point from at least two stations
by measuring angel at one station and distance from other
by measuring distance from two points on traverse line
explain: Distant details, which cannot be directly chained, are located by the method of intersection, measuring angles to the point from at least two known theodolite stations.

q: 9. In precision theodolite traverse for roads and railways, the angular error of closure should not exceed
explain: For a precision theodolite traverse suitable for roads and railways, the permissible angular error of closure is 1 minute multiplied by the square root of the number of stations (N).

q: 10. In any closed traverse, if they survey work is correct, then .............
options: the algebraic sum of latitudes should be equal to zero
the algebraic sum of departures should be equal to zero
the sum of northings should be equal to the sum of southings
explain: For a closed traverse, the sum of latitudes (Northings - Southings) and departures (Eastings - Westings) must both equal zero.

q: 11. In locating the details of inaccessible objects visible at least from transit stations, the method used is .............
options: by angles and distances from the same station
by angle from one station and distance from the other station
by distances from two different stations
explain: Inaccessible objects are often located by observing angles from known stations (intersection method).

q: 12. The traversing by the method of deflection angles is chiefly used in .............
explain: Deflection angle traversing is standard for 'open' traverses like roads, railways, and canals where the route continues forward.

q: 13. In a transit theodolite error due to eccentricity of verniers is counteracted by .............
options: reading different parts of main scale
taking both right swing and left swing reading
explain: Reading both verniers (A and B) and taking the mean value eliminates the error caused by the centers of the graduated circle and the alidade not coinciding.

q: 14. In order to measure the magnetic bearing of a line, the theodolite should be provided with
explain: To measure the magnetic bearing of a line using a theodolite, a small tabular or trough compass must be fitted onto the instrument.

q: 15. Which of the following doesn't involve the method of traversing?
explain: Per this text, tacheometric surveying is identified as not typically involving the specific method of traversing, unlike chain, theodolite, and plane table surveying.

q: 16. The levelling head of a transit theodolite consists of
explain: The leveling head is the entire lower assembly that connects the instrument to the tripod and includes the screws and plates used to level the device.

q: 17. Size of a theodolite is specified by
explain: The 'size' (e.g., a 10 cm theodolite) refers specifically to the graduated diameter of the lower horizontal circle.

q: 18. The latitude and departure of a traverse line are both positive when the whole circle bearing of the line lies in the .............
explain: In the first quadrant (0° to 90°), both sine and cosine values are positive, resulting in positive Latitude (North) and positive Departure (East).

q: 19. The upper plate
options: is attached to the inner spindle and is called vernier plate
has two vernier 180° apart for reading the horizontal angles
is also called alidade of theodolite
explain: The upper plate (vernier plate) carries the verniers and the standards for the telescope and rotates on the inner spindle.

q: 20. If the image formed by the objective of the telescope is not in the plane of cross hairs it is called
explain: Parallax occurs when there is apparent movement between the image and the crosshairs due to the image not falling exactly on the diaphragm plane.

q: 21. The trunion axis or transverse axis is
options: the axis about which the telescope can be rotated in a vertical plane
the axis about which the telescope can be rotated in a horizontal plane
is also known as line of collimation
explain: The trunnion axis is the horizontal axis supported by the standards, allowing the telescope to rotate vertically (transit).

q: 22. Ramsden eye-piece consists of .............
options: two convex lenses short distance apart
two concave lenses short distance apart
one convex lens and one concave lens short distance apart
two plano-convex lenses short distance apart, with the convex surfaces facing each other
explain: A Ramsden eyepiece consists of two identical plano-convex lenses with their curved surfaces facing each other, placed at a distance equal to 2/3 the focal length of one lens.

q: 23. 'SPIRE TEST' is used in permanent adjustment of theodolite for
explain: The Spire Test (or Horizontal Axis Test) ensures that the horizontal axis is perpendicular to the vertical axis.

q: 24. For the locating a distant object visible from two transit stations, the method usually preferred to is .............
options: angles and distance from transit stations
angle from one transit station and distance from the other
explain: When an object is distant or inaccessible, the method of intersection (measuring angles from two known stations) is the most efficient and accurate.

q: 25. The most reliable method of plotting a theodolite traverse is .............
options: by consecutive co-ordinates of each station
by independent co-ordinate of each station
by plotting included angles and scaling off each traverse
by the tangent method of plotting
explain: Independent coordinates (Total Coordinates) are most reliable because errors in plotting one station do not affect the plotting of subsequent stations.

q: 26. A traverse deflection angle is
options: the difference between the included angle and 180°
explain: The deflection angle is the angle between the extension of the previous line and the current line; it is calculated as 180° - Included Angle.

q: 27. The orthographical projection of a traverse leg upon the reference meridian is known, as .............
explain: The projection of a line on the North-South meridian is called the Latitude; the projection on the East-West line is the Departure.

q: 28. The co-ordinate of a point measured perpendicular to the parallel, is called .............
explain: Total latitude is the coordinate of a point measured relative to a reference parallel (usually the Equator or a custom East-West axis).

q: 29. The bearing of the traverse line is calculated by
explain: Bearings can be computed from known starting bearings using either the measured included angles or the deflection angles.

q: 30. The included angle of the theodolite traverse, are generally measured
options: clock wise from the back station
clock wise from the forward station
anti clock wise from the forward station
anti clock wise from the back station
explain: Standard practice is to sight the back station, set zero, and turn clockwise to the forward station.

q: 31. In a closed traverse by included angles, the sum of measured interior angles should be equal to
explain: The formula for the sum of interior angles of a polygon with N sides is (2N - 4) × 90°.

q: 32. The closing error is given by
explain: By Pythagoras' theorem, the magnitude of the closing error is the square root of the sum of the squares of the latitude and departure errors.

q: 33. In a traverse, the algebraic sum of the deflection angles, taking the right hand deflection angles as positive and left hand deflection as negative, should be equal to
explain: In a closed traverse, the sum of the deflection angles must equal 360° to return to the original direction.

q: 34. In closed traverse the algebraic sum of deflection angle is
explain: As noted in Q332, the total turn required to close a loop is a full circle (360°).

q: 35. In a closed traverse, the closing error should not be more than
explain: Errors in angles tend to accumulate in proportion to the square root of the number of stations (√N).

q: 36. If the sum of northing of a traverse exceeds the sum of southing by 2m and sum of easting exceeds the sum of westing by 2m, the resulting closing error will be
explain: Error = √(ΣL² + ΣD²) = √(2² + 2²) = √8 = 2√2 m.

q: 37. The perpendicular distance of the mid point of the line from the reference meridian is known as
explain: Meridian distance of a line is the distance of its midpoint from the reference meridian.

q: 38. The deflection angle may be directly obtained by setting the instrument to read ............ on back station.
explain: By zeroing the theodolite on the back station and then transiting the telescope and turning to the next station, the deflection angle can be read directly.

q: 39. The line of sight is kept as high above ground surface as possible to minimize the error in the observed angles due to
explain: Air layers near the ground are more turbulent and dense, causing light to bend (refraction) and vibrate (shimmering). Raising the line of sight passes the light through more stable air.

q: 40. The distance between terminal points computed from known, as
explain: A traverse base is a line whose length and direction are precisely known or calculated to serve as a reference for the rest of the survey network.

q: 41. When internal angles are to be subtended by a theodolite survey for closed traverse .............
options: exterior angles are measures when the traverse goes anti-clockwise
explain: In a closed traverse, running counter-clockwise results in the measurement of interior angles when observing angles to the right.

q: 42. When the first object is to be focused, the scale is set to 0° 00' 00'' and then .............
options: the upper screw is fixed, lower screw released, the object sighted, lower screw fixed and lower tangent screw operated
both the clamp screw fixed, top tangent screw operated
bottom clamp screw fixed, top screw released, object sighted and upper tangent screw operated
object is exactly bisected by operating both the upper and lower tangent screws whichever is convenient
explain: To keep the initial reading at zero while sighting the first station, the upper plate must be locked to the lower plate (reading 0), and the whole instrument rotated using the lower clamp/tangent screws.

q: 43. The deflection angle may have any value between .............
explain: A deflection angle is the angle between a survey line and the prolongation of the preceding line. It can theoretically range from 0 (straight line) to 180 degrees (reversal).
